newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul Hanbo probe uncovers new suspicions.
newsitem.headline: Seoul Hanbo probe uncovers new suspicions.

text.p: South Korean state prosecutors involved in the probe of a loans scandal surrounding the failed Hanbo Group said Saturday they they suspected that the founder of the failed industrial conflomerate had embezzled about 30 billion won ($33.4 million).

Chung is already standing trial along with nine other people in connection with the scandal after he was arrested in February on charges of fraud and violating laws in issuing cheques and trust and savings companies.
"Embezzlement of the money would be added to Chung's prior charges," a prosecutor said on Saturday.
Investigations were continuing on whether the money suspected of being diverted had been used as bribes to secure bank loans, he said.
On Friday, prosecutors arrested group chairman Chung Bo-keun, son of Chung Tae-soo, and accused him of pocketing about 37 billion won ($41.2 million) from the group's funds.
The junior Chung was also taken into custody in a Seoul detention centre after being questioned at the prosecutors' office.
The group's flagship Hanbo Steel Co. collapsed in January under $5.8 billion ($6.5 million) in largely insecured loans.
The group, with 22 affiliate firms, is South Korea's 14th-largest industrial conglomerate.
Prosecutors reopened their probe into the Hanbo scandal last Friday after the opposition attacked an earlier investigation as a whitewash which failed to bring to justice major players.
Prosecutors said they would seize the Chung family's assets to "end the bad practice of the past when businessmen survived even when their businesses collapsed."

On Thursday, prosecutors said they had so far uncovered family assets of 344 billion won ($383.5 million), which would be seized because of evidence the family evaded taxes of 432.7 billion won ($482.4 million).
